sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the real decision, by when, and which numbers frame it?
criteria: Restates the decision as what enterprise customers see by renewal season (month 6)
Derives the manual queue (16.8M a month) and the bookkeeper hours it costs
Names the enterprise contract clauses as the constraint that decides the case
States at least one thing out of scope

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Covers at least CFO, CPO, sales and legal, each with a distinct want
Says what the CPO gives up (consolidation slips two quarters) and how the trade is agreed
Includes the enterprise customers' controllers and what they need to trust the books
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the real options, and how does each fare on calendar, contracts and cost?
criteria: Includes 'do nothing' as an option
Shows that buying adds a sub-processor, so it needs 90 days' notice and enterprise customers can object
Shows that the fine-tune plan needs 6 engineers when only 4 are free, so it misses the date
Compares options on one table with the same criteria

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you recommend, what do you give up, and what would make you change course?
criteria: Makes one clear recommendation
Names what is given up, including the roadmap slip and the permanent run team
Says whether the decision is reversible and why
Gives a dated revisit with measurable triggers

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What does each option cost over three years, and what is the opportunity cost?
criteria: Compares 3-year totals, not year-one cost
Derives per-transaction model cost from tokens and list prices, including the Sonnet escalation
Separates new spend against the $1.5M cap from engineers already on payroll
Labels assumptions such as run-team size or revenue at risk

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who owns what, during the build and after launch?
criteria: Names a single accountable owner
Splits ownership of the model service and the product experience
Puts threshold and prompt changes behind an eval gate rather than a person

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What is the plan to launch before renewal season, and where can it be stopped?
criteria: Lands GA before renewal season (month 6)
Has at least one gate with a measurable threshold before launch
Starts the beta with renewing enterprise accounts
Includes the month-12 revisit as a milestone

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong at this volume, and what controls it?
criteria: Quantifies wrong postings a month from coverage and precision
Keeps every customer's data in its own context, with no training, and tests it
Has a fallback if the beta fails a gate
Puts the precision floor and opt-in in code or product, not in policy alone

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know it worked, and what would show it is causing harm?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Measures precision of auto-applied postings, not accuracy of all suggestions
Ties at least one metric to renewals or lost-deal notes
Tracks cost per transaction against the revisit trigger

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, and how often?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least four audiences
Tells the CFO new spend and payroll cost separately
Stops sales from promising an accuracy number
Sets a cadence and says failed gates are reported too
